sentences.text: National Insurance Company Limited, ... vs D. Chandrappa And
Another on 17 November, 2023

The Hon'Ble Sri Justice A.V. Ravindra Babu
 M.A.C.M.A. No.1724 Of 2016
Judgment:

-
Challenge in this M.A.C.M.A. is to the award, dated 14.02.2011 in M.V.OP.No.65 of 2005, on the file of District Judge-cum-Chairman, MACT, Chittoor (for short "Tribunal").
The appellant herein is no other than the second respondent.
The first respondent herein is the petitioner/claimant and the second respondent herein is the owner of tipper lorry bearing No.TN-23- D-8572 (for short "offending vehicle") in the above MVOP.

2) The first respondent herein in the capacity of the petitioner laid a claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short "the Act") r/w 455 of AP Motor Vehicles Rules, praying for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- on account of the injuries received by him in a motor vehicle accident which was occurred on 05.07.2003 at about 6-45 p.m., near Mamadugu Cross on Palamaner-Bangalore NH-4 road.
Subsequently, in view of the orders in I.A.No.1196 of 2008, dated 08.07.2009, his prayer for compensation was enhanced to Rs.4,00,000/- from that of Rs.2,00,000/-.
3) The parties to this MACMA will hereinafter be referred to as described before the learned Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

4) The claim of the petitioner, in brief, according to the averments in MVOP No.65 of 2005 is that;
(a) On 05.07.2003 at about 6-45 p.m., the injured and two others, while proceeding on a Hero Honda Motorcycle bearing No.A.P-03-B-6959 and when they reached near Mamadugu Cross on Palamaner-Bangalore NH-4 road, on account of parking of a tipper lorry bearing No.TN-23-D-8572 i.e., offending vehicle in the middle of the road without taking precautions, the motorcycle dashed the offending vehicle, as a result of which, the injured and two others sustained injuries.

They were taken to Government Hospital, Palamaner and from there to CMC Hospital, Vellore, for better treatment.
(b) The Station House Officer, Gangavaram Police Station, registered a case in Crime No.37 of 2003 under Sections 337 and 338 of the Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC") against the driver of the offending vehicle and CC No.380 of 2003 is pending on the file of Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Palamaner.

sentences.text: 1 (c) The injured was treated as inpatient in CMC Hospital, Vellore, for seven days and took treatment and thereafter as an outpatient and incurred Rs.50,000/- towards medicines and treatment.

(d) On account of the fractures, the injured became permanently disabled and unable to attend cultivation and lift weights and lost his income of Rs.200/- per day by doing welding work, besides the monthly income of Rs.3,000/- by selling milk.

(e) The first respondent is the owner and the second respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.
5) The first respondent before the learned Tribunal remained exparte.
6) The 2nd respondent/insurance company before the learned Tribunal filed written statement putting the injured to strict proof of various averments made in the petition and contending that the accident was occurred on account of the negligence of the rider of Hero Honda Motorcycle and that the first respondent-driver parked the offending vehicle by the side of the road margin with proper signals.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of owner and insurer of motorcycle.
The injured is not disabled and that the compensation claimed is excessive.

7) On the basis of the above pleadings, the learned Chairman of the Tribunal settled the following issues for trial:
(1) Whether the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tipper lorry bearing No.TN-23-D-8572 or due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of Hero Honda Motorcycle bearing No.AP 23-B-6959 or both?
(2) Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
(3) Whether the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties?
(4) To what relief?
8) The petitioner before the learned Tribunal examined himself as P.W.1 and further examined P.W.2 and got marked Ex.A.1 to Ex.A.8 and Ex.X.1 and Ex.X.2.
On behalf of the respondents, R.W.1 and R.W.2 were examined and Ex.B.1 was marked.

9) The learned Tribunal on hearing both sides and on considering the oral as well as documentary evidence, answered the issues in favour of the petitioner and awarded compensation of Rs.2,19,100/- with proportionate costs and with subsequent interest at 6% per annum in favour of the petitioner and directed the respondents to deposit the compensation within two months and that on such deposit, the petitioner is permitted to withdraw a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- and remaining compensation amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized Bank for a period of three years.

Therefore, the National Insurance Company Limited, ... vs D. Chandrappa And Another on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156806180/

sentences.text: Tribunal accordingly allowed the claim in part and dismissed the rest of the claim.
Felt aggrieved of the same, the unsuccessful second respondent filed the present MACMA.

10) In view of the contentions advanced, now, in deciding the MACMA, the points that arise for consideration are as follows:
(1) Whether the petitioner before the learned Tribunal proved that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.TN-23-D-8572?
(2) Whether the petitioner proved his entitlement to claim compensation?
(3) Whether the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is just and proper?
(4) To what relief?

Point Nos.1 to 3:
11) The main contention of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant is that the amount of Rs.1,00,000/-
under the head of grievous injuries five in number awarded by the learned Tribunal appears to be excessive and the learned Tribunal should not have granted such an amount when it disbelieved the theory of disability and that this Court may reduce the compensation amount proportionately.
12) As evident from the record though notice is served on the respondent Nos.1 and 2, they did not contest this appeal.
13) P.W.1 is no other than the petitioner, who got filed his chief examination affidavit by adverting to the averments of the claim petition and through his examination Ex.A.1 to Ex.A.8 were marked.
14) P.W.2 is Orthopedic Surgeon, CMC Hospital, Vellore, who treated the injured.
He deposed that the patient by name Chandrappa i.e., petitioner was admitted twice.
First admission was on 06.07.2003 and discharged on 14.07.2003.
Again he was admitted on 05.07.2004 and discharged on 07.07.2004.
The record relating to admission on 05.07.2004 is Ex.X.1.
He was again admitted on 25.09.2005 and discharged on 29.09.2005.
He was operated on 27.09.2005.
Ex . X.2
is the case sheet for admission on 25.09.2005.
As per record, due to infection, the wounds have not been healed.
He cannot say whether the patient was not able to do his normal work due to the injury.
As per the record, patient was admitted in their hospital on four occasions.
Ex.A.4 is the bunch of medical bills issued by their hospital.
15) R.W.1 filed his chief examination affidavit by adverting to the averments of the written statement and through his examination Ex.B.1 was marked.

sentences.text: R.W.2 is no other than the driver of the offending vehicle got filed his chief examination affidavit, deposing that on 05.07.2003 at about 6-45 p.m., near Mamadugu Cross, on Palamaner-Bangalore NH-4, he stopped the offending vehicle on the left side margin of the road with proper signals.

At that time, the rider of the Hero Honda Motorcycle bearing No.AP-03- B-6959 riding the same along with two pillion riders i.e., the petitioner and another person, in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the offending vehicle from back side, as a result, the petitioner and two others fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
The accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle, but not rash and negligent driving of him as the driver of the offending vehicle.

17) Coming to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.TN-2-D-8572 as alleged by the petitioner, the petitioner deposed the same in his chief examination affidavit.
P.W.1 is no other than the injured and he was a witness to the occurrence.
R.W.1, a representative of the second respondent, was not a witness.
It is a fact that R.W.2, the driver of the offending vehicle, is not shown as a party to M.V.O.P.No.65 of 2005.
On the other hand, the first respondent was the owner of the offending vehicle, who did not choose to contest the claim.
However, R.W.2, the driver of the offending vehicle, stepped into the witness box on behalf of the insurance company and deposed in support of the case of the insurance company.

He wanted to disown his responsibility on the ground that he stationed the tipper lorry bearing No.TN-23- D- 8572 on the left side of the road and it is the petitioner, who hit back the offending vehicle by driving with three persons on the motorbike bearing No.AP-03-B-6959.

It is to be noted that according to the case of the petitioner, the offending vehicle was parked in the middle of the road and the accident was occurred in the night without noticing the stationed tipper and parking the tipper in the middle of the road in the night was nothing but negligence.
18) It is to be noted that the petitioner in support of his case got marked certain documents before the Tribunal.

Ex.A.1 is no other than the First Information Report pertaining to Crime No.37 of 2003 under Section 338 of IPC and it reveals that basing on the information furnished by the petitioner, FIR was registered.
Ex . A.2
reveals that it was culminated into filing of the charge sheet.
R.W.2 categorically admitted in cross examination about filing of charge sheet by the investigating officer in C.C.No.380 of 2003 and it is filed against him showing as an accused.

It is to be noted that if really R.W.2 stationed the tipper on the left side margin of the road and if the petitioner really hit back the tipper, R.W.2 being the driver would not have kept quiet, but definitely, he would have lodged a report with the police.
So, it is not a case where R.W.2 acted with a man of reasonable prudent.

19) Having regard to the evidence of P.W.1 and first information submitted by P.W.1 before police which culminated into filing of charge sheet, this Court is of the considered view that the petitioner is able to prove that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle before the Tribunal.
There is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with the second respondent- insurance company.
There is no dispute that the first respondent was the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, in view of the above, both the respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Now, coming to the quantum of compensation, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- in respect of five grievous injuries received by the petitioner @ Rs.20,000/- for each injury and further a sum of Rs.1,19,100/- was awarded under the head of treatment and medicines.

Though the petitioner claimed certain transport expenses and got marked Ex.A.6 and Ex.A.8, but the Tribunal did not consider the same because the petitioner did not examine proper persons in this regard.
21) Coming to the evidence of P.W.1, his evidence is that he received five fracture injuries.

This portion of the evidence of P.W.1 has support from the evidence of P.W.2, Orthopedic Surgeon,
coupled with Ex.A.3-wound certificate and Ex.X.1-attested case-sheet of the petitioner.
The evidence of P.W.2 is very clear about the nature of injuries received by the petitioner.
As seen from Ex.A.3-wound certificate, the petitioner received five grievous injuries.
There is no dispute that the injuries received by the petitioner were treated with surgical intervention which is evident from the evidence of P.W.2.

Though the petitioner pleaded that he sustained disability as per Ex.A.5-disability certificate, but it is a case where the petitioner having marked the documents under Ex.A.4-bunch of medical bills and Ex.X.1 and Ex.X.2 through P.W.2 but did not elicit anything from P.W.2 as to whether they issued Ex.A.5-disability certificate.
These are the circumstances in which the learned Tribunal did not find favour with the case of the petitioner as regards the disability.

Now the contention of the appellant is that when the learned Tribunal disbelieved the theory of disability, it is not justified in awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- each under five grievous injuries.

22) It is to be noted that the injuries received by the petitioner are fractures to distal 3rd shaft of left femur, left ulnar shaft middle third, left radius middle and distal 1/3rd junction, left fibula shaft and comminuted patella.

It is to be noted that simply because the petitioner did not prove the disability,
it cannot be held that the petitioner did not receive the grievous injuries.
Receiving grievous injuries in the form of fractures is one thing and proving of disability on account of such grievous injuries is another thing.
The disability is to be considered to assess the future loss of earnings, etc.

Therefore,
it is not a case where the learned Tribunal awarded any compensation under the head loss of future earnings.
Hence, the very contention of the appellant that when the learned Tribunal disbelieved the theory of disability, it is not justified to award compensation @ Rs.20,000/- for each injury is untenable.
The nature of injuries five in number are nothing but grievous in nature.
They were nothing but multiple fractures treated with surgical intervention.

23) The learned Tribunal relied upon the decision of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad in Ullanki Kanada Durgamma and others vs. Dantuluri Suryanarayana Raju and others 1 to calculate the compensation for five grievous 1997(1) ALD 658 injuries.

sentences.text: As seen from the above said judgment, the High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad took into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court with regard to the grievous injuries.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Having regard to the nature of grievous injuries received by the petitioner and the fact that those were treated with surgical intervention and looking into the pain and suffering which the petitioner felt, this Court is of the considered view that the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal @ Rs.20,000/- for each grievous injuries five in number is absolutely just and reasonable.
The contention of the appellant that the above said compensation i.e., Rs.1,00,000/- for five grievous injuries is excessive cannot be accepted by any stretch of imagination.

There is no dispute about the medical expenditure National Insurance Company Limited, ... vs D. Chandrappa And Another on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156806180/
5 incurred by the petitioner to a tune of Rs.1,19,100/-.

24) Having regard to the above facts and circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that the compensation awarded as above, by the learned Tribunal is just and reasonable and it is not at all excessive.

25) In the light of the findings as referred to above, absolutely, there are no merits in the MACMA,
as such, it is liable to be dismissed.

Point No.4:
26) In the result, the MACMA is dismissed confirming the award, dated 14.02.2011 in M.V.OP.No.65 of 2005, on the file of District Judge-cum-Chairman, MACT, Chittoor.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE A.V. RAVINDRA BABU Dt.17.11.2023.
